decisions.rationale: Artifact exists, artifactId and canonical URL match the sourceRef, and finalUrl is the 2026-04-11 Wayback snapshot while canonicalUrl remains the original The Face article. The declared offsets exactly slice the quoted sentence, and the surrounding retained text identifies the RZA interview discussion as about Shame, supporting the attributed quote.

Artifact exists, artifactId and canonical URL match, and the declared offsets exactly slice the extract. The extract states that except for Method Man and GZA's Clan in da Front, every song has multiple rappers contributing verses, which directly supports the claim.

Artifact exists, artifactId and canonical URL match, and the declared offsets exactly slice the extract. The extract states that the song features RZA production sampling Gladys Knight & the Pips' cover of The Way We Were.

Artifact exists, artifactId and canonical URL match, and the declared offsets exactly slice the extract. The extract states that Method Man wrote his rhymes after hearing Michael Jackson's cover of Come Together by the Beatles and based half of the hook on it.

Artifact exists, artifactId and canonical URL match, and the declared offsets exactly slice the extract. The extract states that Masta Killa wrote his first rhyme ever on the song, supporting the first-ever rhyme claim for Da Mystery of Chessboxin'.

Artifact exists, artifactId and canonical URL match, and the declared offsets exactly slice the extract. In the retained sentence, co-credited follows the preceding co-production-credit phrasing, supporting that Method Man received a co-production credit for Wu-Tang Clan Ain't Nuthing ta F' Wit.
Artifact exists, artifactId and canonical URL match, and the declared offsets exactly slice the extract. The extract directly states that the song was originally titled Lifestyles of the Mega-Rich.

Artifact exists, artifactId and canonical URL match, and the declared offsets exactly slice the extract. The extract directly states that the song was originally recorded over a different beat and with verses in a different order before RZA rearranged them and changed the beat.

Artifact exists, artifactId and canonical URL match, and the declared offsets exactly slice the extract. The extract directly states that Tearz tells two stories: RZA's little brother getting shot and Ghostface Killah recounting a man contracting HIV after unprotected sex.
